lens: Art director judging each V3 grid against @projecttteteatete (PTAT) and the live @naira.flore row. Ten criteria, 1-10 each: (1) the idea is nameable in 3 seconds; (2) a recurring emblem or lockup, fixed in place and legible at 391x521; (3) series architecture; (4) illustration framing real photography; (5) Indian everyday stages; (6) the 12 covers as one grid composition; (7) per-tile legibility at 391x521, with reel covers judged on their centre 3:4 crop (y 240-1680), the 90 px rule and piece size in the grid; (8) rhythm row by row (value, weight, format icons); (9) how row 4 (P3 P2 P1) sits on LAC / flower / BONE; (10) distinctiveness against A, B, PTAT, the category and the other V3 proposals. Calibration on the same ten criteria: A, Naira Matching Centre, scores about 78 (8, 8, 8, 6, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9, 7); B, MANGAL, about 83 (9, 9, 9, 8, 9, 8, 7, 8, 9, 7). Checked against what the renderer does today: the shopfront demo (shutter, tube light, glint) and the CSS 3D box demo (drawer, pop-up) both work, so Galli, Niwas and the Box Theatre extend tested scenes. Drawn From Life's line-drawing reveal is tested, but its AI anatomy plates are not.

scores.proposal: v3-proposal-free.json · NAIRA NIWAS (one building, one window a post)
scores.criteria: 1 Nameable 9: 'a pink building at Diwali, and every post lights one window'. On the finished profile the grid is the building, and every reel opens on that grid at 1/3 scale, so the idea reads before any single tile does. | 2 Emblem 8: the blush kandil hangs at the same x 140 on all 12 covers (about 50x150 px in the grid, a pink shape that works the way PTAT's marigold cluster does), and a brass NAIRA NIWAS plate sits bottom-centre on 11. Both are fixed, and the kandil is true for the whole run (up to Kartik, 24 Nov). Docked one point: the plate's words read at only 21 px, and a festival lamp on every tile drifts toward wallpaper. | 3 Series 9: storeys are weeks (shops, first floor, second floor, terrace) and flat numbers are post titles. Residents recur: 101 Aai, 103 the siblings, 202, 203, through P3's gift tags, P8's chit, P9's lost earring and P10's earring card. It is the only V3 with a cast and a memory. | 4 Illustration + photo 8: a drawn Deco facade frames real cut-outs, held at a stated true relative scale beside one prop. Docked because each tile mixes three registers: flat SVG building, photoreal AI props (soap dish, brass vati, desk corner, mirror, glasses) and the box render. 18 AI plates. | 5 Stages 9: present-day housing-society life that no option has used: the watchman's desk, LOST: ONE EARRING by the lift, the spare-key neighbour, the disputed window seat, tamarind and lemon, kahi nako on Padwa, the borrowed necklace, the terrace rehearsal, wedding lights down the facade. | 6 Grid composition 9: the strongest grid idea in the tournament. Twelve bays make one building, and pilasters and string courses run across every joint. The storeys darken from lit shops to wedding night, the terrace row shares one sky and one string-light wire, and the real wordmark crowns r1c1. Docked: blush plaster fills about 50% of every tile, so colour lives only in the openings. On two of every three rollout days the grid is shifted mid-week and the building mis-stacks. | 7 Legibility 8: headlines are 88-120 px (32-43 px in the grid) inside the opening, and where it matters the headline is an object: P1's tent card, and P9's notice with LOST: at 150 px (54 px in the grid). Pieces are mostly 130-190 px in the grid. Exception: P6's cover has no Velista line, and its bracelet reads as a thin line cut off by both window edges. | 8 Rhythm 8: openings alternate L D L / D L D up the building. Column 3 is all reels and column 2 all carousels, so the icons form bands. Rows 1-3 each have one breathing tile, and the darkness climbs with the calendar. The shared facade softens the checkerboard. | 9 Transition 8: a lac #42060E pavement sampled from LAC runs along the foot of row 4, so the building stands on the August row. The openings run light/dark/light over dark/light/dark, and the first new words above BONE are BACK IN 5 MINUTES. | 10 Distinctiveness 8: a Bombay-Deco co-op society is unclaimed in Indian demi-fine and far from A's counter and B's Mummy's house. 'The grid is one picture' is a known Instagram trope, saved here because every tile is complete on its own. Its register overlaps Galli almost entirely.
best_posts: P9 LOST: ONE EARRING. The notice by the lift is the headline (LOST: at 150 px = 54 px in the grid, the most legible type tile of any V3). Amethyst huggies on the sill give the grid its lilac note. The lift gate concertinas in the loop. Pure society humour.

P1 BACK IN 5 MINUTES. The oldest tent card in Indian retail owns the 76-day silence ('eleven weeks, actually. new stock came in.'). The Ruby bracelet is 188 px in the grid, directly above BONE, and the reel teaches the whole system by opening on the dark building.

P12 EVEN THE BUILDING DRESSED UP. Wedding lights unfurl down all twelve bays and the camera pulls back to the finished profile: the system pays off as motion. The real wordmark on the corner tower makes the top-left tile carry the brand name.
P7 काही नको. / AND HE BELIEVED HER. Two scripts, one deadpan Marathi beat and a self-purchase ending. The curtain draws and the real box drawer slides out in the site's own 1.1 s.
P3 THE WATCHMAN KNOWS. A gift guide told from the gate, with four tagged boxes and the cast introduced (101, 202, 203, YOU). It lands on 1 Nov, in time for Diwali delivery.
weakest_posts: P6 NO OIL. NO WICK. On Diwali, the season's biggest day, the cover has no Velista headline (only शुभ दीपावली at 56 px). The Rivière Eternal reads as an 18 px-stone thread cut off by both window edges, and the panatis add a second festive cue to the kandil.
P11 THE MOON IS BACK. The season's second moon and the weakest joke (a callback that needs P2's context). The Baroque Shell is fine but the tile adds nothing new to the top row.

P5 TAMARIND AND LEMON. A photoreal AI brass vati on AI newsprint and cloth, satin huggies with a deliberately soft glint, and 'made to stay gold.' in a Dhanteras caption. The most AI-dependent still life.
P4 WINDOW SEAT: STILL DISPUTED. The joke needs the chalk line to read, and the AI striped cushion carries the tile. Strong as a sibling send, thin as a thumbnail.
must_fix: Mock all 12 covers at 391x521 above LAC / flower / BONE, plus the two mid-week shifted states, before building. If the blush facade reads monotone, enlarge or deepen the opening fields. Every tile must stand complete when the grid is shifted.
P6: give the cover a Velista headline and a piece that reads at thumbnail, and keep one cue beside the kandil (see recommendation).

Brand mark: P1's fascia sets 'NAIRA PETITE' and 11 plates set 'NAIRA NIWAS' in Velista. A typed NAIRA next to a real wordmark risks reading as a redrawn logo. Use the kit wordmark on P1's fascia and get the owner's call on the typed plates (the proposal's own fallback).

Wording: 'emerald-green' (P9, P12 end card 'THE EMERALD-GREEN SET') must become 'green' or 'green cubic zirconia' per the brief. Drop 'made to stay gold.' from the Dhanteras (P5) and Diwali (P6) captions.

The kandil plus the flower ghost on all twelve tiles bends the brand's flower rule and the one-cue rule (P2 bangle wall, P6 panatis). It needs an owner sign-off, with the four-petal jaali fallback ready.
P3's WhatsApp number promises the staffed matching service that was A's open question. Confirm staffing or drop the line.
P12: confirm the Emerald variants on 21 Nov and the 36 cm necklace length on the PDP.
graftable: The establishing shot: every reel opens on the profile grid at 1/3 scale and lights one window. It is the most grid-aware motion idea in the tournament and works for any grid-composed option.
LOST: ONE EARRING (P9), the notice as headline, for any feed that needs a huggie post.
काही नको. / AND HE BELIEVED HER. (P7) as a Padwa self-purchase line.
The recurring residents (101, 103, 202, 203) as a memory device across posts.
The green-set finale as the ruby fallback for A or B, whose Ruby variants sell about one a day.

scores.proposal: v3-proposal-illustrated-films.json · DRAWN FROM LIFE (twelve small films)
scores.criteria: 1 Nameable 8: 'drawings of an Indian moment where only the jewellery is real'. Violet line on coloured paper plus one photographed piece reads at a glance, and P1's cover names the series in 108 px. | 2 Emblem 6: the signed margin (N° 07/12, a Cormorant inscription, the wordmark as signature) is consistent but typographic and small. Its 26 px and 36 px type become 9-13 px in the grid, and the wordmark 64 px. Nothing reads as a mark the way MILNI, B's seal or Niwas's kandil does, and the horizon line and paper halo are devices, not an emblem. | 3 Series 8: N° 01/12 editions; Tuesday/Friday films and Sunday flipbooks; four chapters (before, Diwali, between, weddings); one four-beat grammar and one sign-off ('the moment goes. the piece stays.'). No named sub-series. | 4 Illustration + photo 9: the purest answer to PTAT's drawn frame around a real thing. Everything is drawn except the piece, behind a 14 px paper halo, and a drawn shape visibly becomes the photograph: the lamp trail becomes the ruby bracelet, the rangoli line the Prism, the safety pins the Duo Link. Docked one point because 7 covers rely on AI line plates of heads, hands, necks and ears, the anatomy the judges warned about. | 5 Stages 9: the most intimate and specific set of moments: Sunday plait, aukshan thali, faral in a steel tiffin, brass polishing, rangoli, R.S.V.P., the tailor's 'gala kaisa chahiye?', mehendi drying, safety pins in the pleats, jhumkas off at 2 a.m. | 6 Grid composition 8: a perfect value checkerboard with mirror-symmetric jewel nights (oxblood r1c1/r3c3, green r1c3/r3c1, a violet spine down column 2). One horizon line runs at the same height across every row, and the margins align like framed prints. Docked: 3.2 px violet lines on pale day papers drop to about 1.2 px at 36%, which risks a wall of pale paper. | 7 Legibility 7: headlines are 84-120 px, top-left on every tile, and pieces 85-230 px in the grid. The most-seen top-left tile shows a 90 px huggie beside a drawn jhumka, and fine line art loses detail at thumbnail size. | 8 Rhythm 9: every row has one night tile, one airy day film and one dense tile. Sunday carousels run down column 1 and reels down columns 2-3, so the format icons form two clean bands, and each row is one week's chapter. | 9 Transition 9: P3 sage day over LAC; P2 a violet night with small stars directly above the cream flower tile, its negative; P1 blush over BONE. LAC's oxblood returns at P4 and P12, and the Velista headlines top-left echo LAC and BONE's big serif words. | 10 Distinctiveness 8: visually far from A, B and every Indian demi-fine grid. But three ideas repeat A: P2 'THE MOON IS LATE' vs A P2 'THE MOON IS ALWAYS LATE', P9's neckline guide vs A's graft G1, and P7 'kisne diya? maine' vs A P3's slide.
best_posts: P4 RED, LIKE THE TILAK. The aukshan thali circles, its lamp trail closes into an ellipse that becomes the Ruby Baguette bracelet, and the kumkum is the same red. The best rhyme in the tournament, on oxblood, built to forward.

P6 A RANGOLI LASTS ONE NIGHT. Pastel rangoli on bottle green with the Prism laid along its border, then a broom that sweeps everything but the bracelet. The strongest colour tile and the thesis as a Diwali joke.
P8 R.S.V.P. A one-word 120 px headline (43 px in the grid), 'nobody does. everybody comes.', and the card's linked-ring monogram becomes the Bold Nocturne Drops.
P12 THE HEAVY ONES COME OFF AT 2 A.M. The season's thesis told as a scene on the top-left tile. Its last slide is a storyboard of all twelve films.
P11 NOBODY SEES THE SAFETY PINS. Two-metal pins slide to the wrist and become the two-tone Duo Link: a product truth told as a joke.
weakest_posts: P2 THE MOON IS LATE. Nearly A's P2 headline word for word, it rests on a silhouette from an AI anatomy plate, and the moon is absent from its own cover.
P10 MEHENDI'S DRYING. The most anatomy of any cover (two raised palms, an ear, a second person's fingers) carrying a single 110 px earring.
P9 GALA KAISA CHAHIYE? A neck-and-collarbones plate in a mirror, and the same neckline-guide idea as A's graft G1.
P1 MUMMY'S PLAIT. The key art depends on AI head-and-hands plates and a 2.4x push to an ear. The idea is right, but this is the riskiest build to post first.
must_fix: Give the series a thumbnail-legible emblem. The signed margin cannot carry recognition at 391x521: add one fixed mark at 90 px or more (for example a N° roundel or a paper-halo label in the same corner on all 12 covers), or set the wordmark signature larger.
Thicken the key contours on covers to 5-6 px. Every day cover needs its 35-45% wash field so pale papers do not read empty in the grid.
Cut the overlaps with A: rewrite P2's line, replace P9's neckline guide, and do not reuse 'kisne diya? maine' on P7.
Anatomy: render P1 first from the AI line plates, reject anything that reads generated, and keep the agent-drawn single-line fallback ready for P2, P9, P10 and P12.
The flower cameo hidden in every film bends the brand's flower rule. Owner's call; delete it if in doubt.
Confirm the 36 cm necklace length (P9, P12) on the PDP.
graftable: The rhyme: a drawn everyday shape match-dissolves into the photographed piece. This is 'Anaar, pre-peeled.' as a motion device, and it suits any option's reels.
The 14 px paper halo rule (drawing never touches the jewellery) as an honesty-and-craft device.
P4's aukshan thali and lamp-trail bracelet as a Bhaubeej reel.
P6's rangoli flipbook with the broom gag as a Diwali carousel.
P12's storyboard-of-the-season last slide, and the sign-off 'the moment goes. the piece stays.'

scores.proposal: v3-proposal-galli.json · NAIRA GALLI (one lane, twelve shops)
scores.criteria: 1 Nameable 9: 'a street of little Indian shops, each selling one Naira piece'. Shop names on 920x230 boards at 104-120 px (38-43 px in the grid) name every tile instantly. | 2 Emblem 8: a municipal street plate (नायरा गल्ली / NAIRA GALLI / N° 01 · SHUTTERS UP) is nailed at the same coordinates on all 12 covers and every end card, 130x65 px in the grid. The green plate shape reads; its words do not. The painted shutter end card is a second, motion-native lockup that makes every loop seamless. | 3 Series 9: Shop N° 01-12, and four hour-series that are also the four rows (SHUTTERS UP, LAMPS LIT, AFTER FOUR, OPEN LATE). | 4 Illustration + photo 8: Bombay-Deco elevations frame real pieces in their windows. Docked for photoreal AI steel, press, baskets, sugarcane and box camera mixed into flat SVG, and for twelve facades that must look like one hand. | 5 Stages 9: the bangle-wala's soap, the money order's 'buy something nice', the bartan bhandar, the electricals ladi, the optician's chart, the general store's jars, the co-op bank's pen on a chain, the card press, the phoolwala, the stage photo, all in the Puneri shop-sign voice. | 6 Grid composition 8: each row shares one 3,240 px sky and pavement, so it reads as one street, and the four hours alternate pale and dark bands. The facades form a checkerboard. Docked: the street aligns only when a row is complete, and twelve near-identical facade templates make a wall of shopfronts rather than a picture. | 7 Legibility 6: only the shop name reads. The joke sits on a pati at 44-64 px (16-23 px in the grid), under the brief's 90 px rule. Pieces sit small inside dense windows (P8's bracelet about 36 px inside its jar, P11's studs, P4's bangle on a ledge), behind board, pati, toran, diyas, steps, kerb, road and plate. | 8 Rhythm 8: dawn, dusk, afternoon and night bands, one dense, one mid and one breathing shop per row, and column 3 as the reel column. But no tile truly breathes: every one carries the full facade stack. | 9 Transition 8: row 4's road is LAC's own #42060E and runs straight down into LAC and BONE, and the facades go light/dark/light over dark/light/dark. | 10 Distinctiveness 7: Indian and specific, but pastel symmetrical shopfronts are a well-worn illustration trope. A already owns 'the shop' (a signboard bookend and a counter), and Niwas covers the same Deco register with a stronger grid idea. Its Karwa Chauth bangle-soap joke is also Niwas's P2.
best_posts: P7 OPTICIANS · READ THE LAST LINE. A spectacles-shaped parapet, an eye chart whose rows spell NAIRA GALLI, a last line of real 2.5 mm stones and a loupe: craft proof as a joke, with the clearest silhouettes in the set.

P4 POST OFFICE · BUY SOMETHING NICE. The money order fills itself in at ₹999, the bangle's exact price. A ruby pillar box gives the strongest silhouette, and it posts 8 days before Bhaubeej, built to forward.
P9 CO-OP BANK · PLEASE RETURN THE PEN. (the chain, you can keep.) The best product rhyme, and the first hero tile for the 79-unit Toggle chain.
P1 NAIRA · BACK AFTER LUNCH. The plate is unveiled, three shutters go up in a wave, and the real wordmark sits on the house's board with the Ruby bracelet large in the window.
P12 PHOTO STUDIO · ONE WITH THE WHOLE FAMILY. The baguette family posed tall to small on risers, with a photo envelope as the bill.
weakest_posts: P5 BARTAN BHANDAR. The densest tile: nine-plus AI steel vessels in mirror symmetry, with the Heartbead small in a niche. The tile most likely to read AI-made and cluttered.
P11 PHOOLWALA. AI baskets, sugarcane and toran heaped round a small stud pair on a leaf. The densest tile in the top row, and 'still fresh on Monday' is a soft joke.
P8 GENERAL STORES. The Prism sits inside a glass jar at about 100 px (36 px in the grid), and it reuses the paid 'almost edible' candy frame.
P10 WEDDING CARDS. Press, type cases, toran and ladi crowd the cuff on a night facade.
must_fix: Make the joke readable in the grid: set the pati headline at 90 px or more on covers, or accept that only the shop name reads and move the line into the first video beat.
Strip the cover stack to board + piece + plate + one prop (the proposal's own fallback), and set a floor for the piece (about 300 px long at 1080).
Replace the dense AI steel shelf (P5) and baskets (P11) with flat SVG silhouettes if they read photoreal against the flat facades.
Rows break whenever a week is part-posted. Each tile must stand on its own, and the shifted states must be tested before posting.
Verify P4's India Security Press line before use, and confirm North Star and Petal Flower Studs stock (10 per metal) the evening before.
graftable: P7's eye chart, last line and loupe as a craft-proof reel for any option.
P4's money order with 'buy something nice' and the amount equal to the price, as a Bhaubeej gift post.
P3's earring cards printed 'ACTUAL SIZE.' on a ruler drawn to the same scale.
P9's 'PLEASE RETURN THE PEN. (the chain, you can keep.)'.
The shutter-down end card that makes every reel loop seamlessly.
Row strips (one shared sky and pavement per row) for any grid that composes by row.

scores.criteria: 1 Nameable 8: 'the pink Naira box that opens into a tiny theatre'. The box, footlights, curtain and titles such as PLEASE TAKE YOUR SEATS, ENCORE and THE FINALE read as theatre, though at a glance some will read it as unboxing. | 2 Emblem 9: the real blush box sits at the same size and place on 11 covers (about 215 px wide in the grid), with the real wordmark on its lid at about 135 px: the most legible brand mark in the tournament. The ticket stub (SHOW 01-12, प्रयोग) numbers the run. | 3 Series 9: Season One, SHOW 01-12, matinee vs night show, programme end cards, and a playbill of all twelve shows on the finale. | 4 Illustration + photo 7: cut-paper flats, a CSS 3D box and real pieces: more paper craft than drawing. The jewellery is a small actor on a stage only about 212 px deep, and the laser-cut arch, elephants, chairs, karwa and three gouache backdrops are the AI plates most likely to read AI-made. | 5 Stages 8: the karwa on a terrace, the locker wall, the one dead bulb on the ladi, Tree 3 at annual day, the front row of wedding chairs, the invitation that came in a box. Witty, but every Indian object is miniaturised behind a theatre device. | 6 Grid composition 8: a shelf of twelve theatres. One shelf line at y 1046 runs across each row and survives mid-week shifts, the only grid idea here that does. Three colour columns (lac/blush, a lilac aisle, sage/green) form a value checkerboard, matinee-light and night-dark tiles match their posting times, and opening and closing curtains bookend the long diagonal. | 7 Legibility 6: titles at 104 px read, but the jewellery often does not. P3's pieces sit in W 300 boxes; P8's earrings are two leaves on a cardboard tree; P9's huggies are 'one red and one green dot'; P10's drops are 70x150. P1, the first new tile above BONE, shows no piece at all. | 8 Rhythm 7: the value alternates, but the same box in the same place eleven times, and a fixed dense > mid > quiet order left to right in every row, make every row the same sentence. The proposal flags this sameness itself. | 9 Transition 8: P3 pale blush over LAC; P2 a lilac night over the flower tile, with NAIRA's flower-as-I on the lid directly above it; P1 sage over BONE. The lac column starts and ends in lac. | 10 Distinctiveness 9: no one else can own the real Naira box, which the owner already tuned on the site, and packaging is the account's one breakout topic.
best_posts: P6 ONE BULB IS ALWAYS OUT. Two swags of paper bulbs cross the whole red tile, one stays dark, and the Fine Tennis Bracelet's stones chase like a ladi. The best thumb-stop and joke in the set.
P8 YOU WERE TREE 3. A nervous cardboard tree gets the lead on Children's Day: the funniest motion in the tournament and a comment prompt ('tree, cloud, villager 2?').
P4 HE WILL NEVER SAY THE LINE. A typed Bhai Dooj script with 'Didi, I love y' struck out, a pop-up heart and the Heartbead. Tender and very sendable.
P12 THE FINALE. CAST OF THREE. The curtain call of the Ruby set on lac at top-left answers P1's curtain on the long diagonal, and it carries a playbill of the season.
P1 PLEASE TAKE YOUR SEATS. The quietest, most premium key art: a shut box with a line of light at the drawer (but see must-fix).
weakest_posts: P9 THE FRONT ROW SEES IT ALL. Four AI wedding chairs in front of two huggies that read as 'one red and one green dot' at 391 px.
P3 FOUR BOXES. A tower of W 300 boxes: the pieces in the drawers are 40-75 px in the grid, so the tile reads as packaging, not jewellery.
P7 ENCORE. A 560x160 painted bioscope scroll (three AI gouache plates) and a chain on a small paper bust: too small to read on the cover.
P11 THE CARD CAME IN A BOX. The laser-cut arch and elephants are the AI props most likely to look generated.
must_fix: P1's cover has no jewellery. The first new tile above BONE must show a piece: open the drawer a little and put the Prism on stage, or set it on the lid's front edge.
Set a floor for the piece on every cover (about 300 px long at 1080, about 108 px in the grid), or push in on the stage for covers. Drop the cover sets that can't meet it (P3, P8, P9).

Break the sameness: take two or three covers to a close stage view without the full box (the proposal's own P7/P10 fallback), and stop the fixed dense > mid > quiet column order so that weight zigzags.
Wording: 'Emerald' as a stone or variant word in captions (P2 'in Ruby, Crystal or Emerald', P9 'one Ruby, one Emerald') must become 'green'.
The karwa wearing a bracelet touches a ritual object (owner's call), and 'the understudy' (P5) may read as second-best.
The CSS 3D face-sorting risk: check every 10th frame, and keep the 2D compositing fallback ready.
graftable: P6 'ONE BULB IS ALWAYS OUT.' (a ladi with one dark bulb, and a tennis bracelet whose stones chase like bulbs) for any Diwali tile.
P8 'YOU WERE TREE 3.' for Children's Day.
P4's struck-out script for Bhai Dooj.
The real box drawer opening in the site's 1.1 s as an end card or reveal in any option.
Three soft bells as the series' sound signature.
The playbill / season-index last slide.

beats_A_and_B: NAIRA NIWAS: YES, beats both. On this lens it clears A (about 78) on world, series, motion and grid-as-picture, and edges B (about 83). The profile itself becomes the artwork, every reel opens on that grid, and its present-day co-op society wit is fresher than B's Mummy's-house nostalgia. It trails B only on raw colour saturation and multi-script thumb-stop. DRAWN FROM LIFE: beats A clearly (illustration depth, motion, transition, rhythm) and is level with B. It is better in premium craft and in the piece-as-punchline rhyme, worse on emblem (nothing reads at thumbnail where B's seal does), and three of its ideas repeat A. It beats B only if its emblem fix lands. NAIRA GALLI: beats A on world and Indian depth, but not B. Its jokes sit on 44-64 px patis the grid cannot read, its tiles are as dense as MANGAL's were before the judges cut it, and Niwas does the same Deco register with a stronger grid. THE BOX THEATRE: beats A on emblem, distinctiveness and motion, but not B at grid level. Eleven identical box placements and pieces too small on stage lose to B's variety and thumb-stop, even though its emblem beats B's seal.
recommendation: Build NAIRA NIWAS as Variation 3. Under the reference-grid lens it is the only proposal whose grid is itself a composition (twelve bays, one building, the real wordmark on the crown at top-left) and whose motion is grid-native (each reel opens on the profile and lights one window). It also has a fixed emblem, a recurring cast and a run of present-day Maharashtrian society jokes that neither A nor B touches. Before render: (1) Rebuild P6, the weakest cover on the biggest day, by grafting THE BOX THEATRE's P6 onto 101's balcony: 'ONE BULB IS ALWAYS OUT.' as a Velista headline, a ladi with one dark bulb, and the Rivière Eternal (or Fine Tennis) laid along the ledge, whose glint chases like the bulbs. Drop the panatis, so the tile carries one cue beside the kandil. (2) Put the kit wordmark on P1's fascia instead of typed NAIRA PETITE, and get the owner's call on 'NAIRA NIWAS' set in Velista on 11 plates. (3) Write 'green cubic zirconia' and 'THE GREEN SET', never 'emerald-green', and drop 'made to stay gold.' from the Dhanteras and Diwali captions. (4) Mock all 12 covers at 391x521 above LAC / flower / BONE, plus the two mid-week shifted states, before building. If the blush facade reads monotone, enlarge or deepen the opening fields. (5) Get the owner's sign-off on the kandil and flower ghost appearing on every tile, with the jaali fallback ready. Further grafts: GALLI's 'ACTUAL SIZE.' ruler on the back of P10's blank earring card (the card is already there), and DRAWN FROM LIFE's storyboard-of-the-season as P12's last carousel-style still or end-card beat (all twelve windows as one contact sheet). P11's second moon is the next weakest tile; give the terrace a non-moon joke if one tests better. Runner-up, for an owner who wants the quietest and most premium V3: DRAWN FROM LIFE, provided it gets a thumbnail-legible emblem (one fixed mark at 90 px or more on every cover), thicker cover contours and new ideas for P2, P7 and P9 that do not repeat A. Do not take GALLI and NIWAS forward together: they are the same Bombay-Deco register, and Niwas carries it better.
